title: Cleaning equipment care, vacuums and cleaning-tool hazards
audience: Cleaning and support workers who maintain vacuums, cloths and shared equipment in healthcare settings.
learningOutcomes: Select a vacuum that controls dust and state the bag-changing rule.
Describe how a shared, non-disposable item is cleaned between clients.
Name five hazards in cleaning equipment work and a control for each.

instruction.heading: Choosing a vacuum that controls dust
instruction.body: Dust is a route for organisms, so a vacuum must have suitable suction and must not release dust and bacteria back into the air. The guide gives two options: a correctly vented or ducted vacuum, or a dust-holding mop used with detergent solution. Never use a vacuum to pick up clinical waste. Carpets need daily vacuuming, so the machine must be working properly before the day begins.

instruction.heading: Vacuum upkeep and bag changing
instruction.body: Dispose of a full vacuum bag without spilling its contents, and replace it with a clean one. Do not overfill a bag and do not reuse it. Clean the filters and the cleaning heads regularly, and check that the cleaning head is free of hair and debris before use. A neglected machine throws dust into the air, so keeping it in good order is part of infection control, not an extra job.

instruction.heading: Cloths and reusable shared items
instruction.body: Launder cloths after each use, and discard any that cannot be washed. Take a fresh cloth into every new area. Reusable mop heads are washed hot after each use. Non-disposable items, for example stethoscopes, medical equipment, hoists, slings, walking frames, trolleys and trays, are cleaned between each client. Use the manufacturer instructions for the product and method, and check the product before you apply it, because the manufacturer may list unsuitable methods and products. Protective wraps and covers can shield awkward items like keyboards, and each one is replaced between clients.

instruction.heading: Hazards in cleaning equipment work
instruction.body: The guide lists five hazards: slippery wet ground, liquid reaching powered equipment, heavy lifting, vapours from chemicals or spilt products, and irritation of the skin caused by chemicals. Control them by signing wet areas and drying floors, keeping water and liquids away from electrical equipment, asking for help or using lifting aids for heavy items, ventilating and reading the product label for fumes, and wearing gloves suited to the chemical. Check the manufacturer instructions before cleaning any electrical item.

procedure: Check the vacuum filter and bag before use, and replace a full bag without spilling.
Use the method and product the facility lists for the surface.
Clean each shared, non-disposable item between clients using the manufacturer method.
Launder reusable cloths, and discard any cloth that cannot be washed.
Store equipment clean and dry, and report any hazard you find with the location.

workedExamples.situation: While finishing a clinic corridor, a cleaner notices the vacuum bag is full.
workedExamples.reasoning: Close the full bag without spilling any dust, dispose of it through the facility waste route, and fit a new bag. Check the filter at the same time. Do not overfill or reuse the bag.

workedExamples.situation: A hoist sling needs cleaning between residents, and the cleaning room holds a bleach product.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Is the bleach product the right choice?
workedExamples.reasoning: Not without checking. The manufacturer instructions for the sling list the suitable products and methods, and the facility list governs. Ask the supervisor before using any product on it.

equipmentAndPpe: Vacuum with suitable suction and a vented or ducted design, and spare bags
Gloves suited to the product, and heavy-duty gloves where needed

commonErrors.error: Overfilling a vacuum bag or reusing it.
commonErrors.prevention: Replace the bag before it is full and dispose of it intact.
Use the waste procedure for clinical waste, and never use the vacuum for it.

commonErrors.error: Cleaning a shared item with a dry cloth.
commonErrors.prevention: Use the approved wet method from the manufacturer instructions.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Check the manufacturer instructions before cleaning any electrical item, and keep liquids away from power points.
Ask for help or use a lifting aid for heavy equipment, in line with the workplace manual handling procedure.
Completing this lesson does not grant a licence, certificate or authority to perform regulated work.

qualityStandard: Learner names the two vacuum options and the bag-changing rule.
Learner describes the between-client clean for a shared item in order.
Learner names five hazards and a control for each.
documentationEvidence: Equipment check record showing the vacuum filter and bag were checked and changed.
Hazard report for any equipment defect or hazard found.
summary: A vacuum must control dust, and its bags are changed without spilling.
Shared, non-disposable items are cleaned between clients by the manufacturer method.
Cleaning equipment carries hazards that are controlled by signs, drying, lifting aids and product labels.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which approach reduces dust released by a vacuum in a healthcare setting?
options: A vacuum with suitable suction and a vented or ducted design
Vacuuming with the bag left open and the filter removed
Blowing dust out of the room through the open door and window
Vacuuming clinical waste bags in the same room as the patient

knowledgeChecks.question: How should a non-disposable item such as a walking frame be handled between clients?
options: Wiped with a dry cloth once a week and then put away for the next patient
Cleaned between clients using the manufacturer method and an approved product
Left for a week before the next clean and then used by the next client
Shared without cleaning because it is low risk and it is used by many clients

knowledgeChecks.question: Which is one hazard listed for cleaning equipment work?
options: Vapours from chemicals or from spilt products
Cleaning in daylight with the lights on
Using a microfibre cloth on the wet floor
Working in a team with a shared cloth today
